reason: E1 and E2 support the general concept that an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves ductility while maintaining strength in a specific Al-containing RHEA, but the hypothesis applies this to the different alloy NbMoTaW without evidence that B2 precipitates can form in this system, and the claim about irradiation resistance is entirely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Inverted BCC+B2 microstructure with discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix improves room-temperature ductility in RHEAs
The ductility improvement is due to the continuous matrix being the ductile BCC phase rather than the ordered B2 phase
The inverted microstructure maintains high yield strength at room and elevated temperatures
The specific heat treatment (solutionizing at 1400°C, lower-temperature anneal) can produce this inverted microstructure in a BCC+B2 RHEA
Nanoscale B2 precipitates do not significantly alter irradiation resistance
